rv.q: I braced, I flinched, and then, to my surprise and delight ... I applauded. Repeatedly.
But if Bring It On doesn’t offer much depth, it does hit impressive heights.
"Bring It On: The Musical" has more – more athletics, more songs, more dazzle, more interesting characters.

Is the show destined for a place in the musical-theater pantheon? Unlikely. But it scores points by reinventing rather than replicating the source material, sampling from a tasty selection of pop-cultural favorites.
Strong performances from a personable cast, athletically impressive staging and an engaging score combine to make “Bring It On” a pert and refreshing summer surprise.
The precision and daring with which they fling themselves into the air and engage in breathtaking runs of back flips across the wide St. James stage give the musical a real kick.
All fluff, and with an edge of satire, the show is nonetheless lots of fun.
"Bring It On" doesn't break new ground, but it kept me smiling.
The show would probably feel more at home at Madison Square Garden than on the stage of the St. James Theatre.

cn.t: This cheerleading musical delivers entertaining acrobatics and energetic performances that overcome familiar plotting, offering a frothy but fun teen confection that aims modest and mostly succeeds.

sg.ra: Closest and most direct view of the stage at St. James Theatre, with the fullest sound. The standard top pick for any show here.
An elevated, full-stage view with no orchestra-level neck-craning — especially strong for shows with big staging or choreography.
A modest side angle on the stage but still close and clear — a reliable choice when center seats are sold out.
Farther from the stage than center orchestra — less up-close, but the sound still carries well.
At 1,710 seats, St. James Theatre is one of the larger Broadway houses — far side mezzanine seats sit well off-axis and a long way from the stage.

vs.sum: The St. James Theatre offers good sightlines for most seats, though the lack of a solid rake can be an issue if someone tall sits in front of you. The sound quality is generally good, but the tight legroom can be uncomfortable for taller patrons. The theater's ambiance is enhanced by its historic and grand interior, while facilities are average with standard amenities.

acc.note: No steps from sidewalk to Orchestra. No elevator. Mezzanine up 29 steps, Balcony up 76 steps.
